hypotheses.reasoning: Redis restarted at 20:08:17 after node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it started empty. Order-service cache miss ratio jumped to 95% (baseline 2%), and every checkout read fell through to postgres as SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = $1. Postgres connections reached 491/500 with CPU at 94-98%, queries slowed to 2.5-8.3s, and order-service orders queries began timing out at 5s. The api-gateway 504s are downstream symptoms. The trigger (a cache restart) is survivable alone; the stampede onto the database turned it into the outage. Postgres vacuum and checkpoints look normal and payment-svc is healthy, so neither is the cause. The payment-svc connection reset at #33 is minor and was retried.

The postgres connection pool (477-491 of 500) is near its limit and CPU is saturated. This is the saturated resource, but it was driven by the cache-miss load rather than being the origin, so it is a weaker reading of the same lines.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore redis cache capacity and warm it, and enable RDB persistence or a replica so restarts don't start empty. Short term, throttle or coalesce order-service reads on cache miss, and cap or raise the postgres connection pool to relieve saturation. Add an alert on cache miss ratio. Confirm that checkout 504s recover as the miss ratio returns to baseline.
